data.title: Musk says Tesla Cybertruck demand is outpacing production
data.description:
Tesla (TSLA) CEO Elon Musk said on Saturday that his company’s manufacturing capacity is unable to keep up with order backlog for its Cybertruck before the EV maker winds down its production next year.

The billionaire investor on Friday announced that the production of the stainless-steel pickup will come to a halt at the company’s Texas gigafactory in mid-2027 to make room for its Cybercab robotaxi.

With Musk calling it an “end of an era” for the vehicle, car enthusiasts expected the Cybertruck to become a prized collector's item in the years to come, sparking renewed interest given its futuristic design.

“The Tesla Cybertruck order backlog is currently far more than we can make before dismantling the line for Cybercab expansion around June/July next year,” Musk wrote on X, noting that the company is adding an extra shift to ship all deliveries on time. "We will add an extra shift to try to get all orders done in time," he said.

data.title: Nvidia CEO was romantically involved with alleged Chinese spy, U.S. memo says: FT
data.description:
The Trump administration believes Nvidia’s (NVDA) CEO, Jensen Huang, had a romantic relationship with a Chinese woman who allegedly served China’s main intelligence agency as a spy, The Financial Times reported on Saturday, citing a government memo.

Based on information obtained by American intelligence, U.S. officials wrote the memo earlier this year stating that Huang had been romantically involved with Alice Huang, an executive at a Singapore-based client of the chipmaker, according to people familiar with the matter.

U.S. intelligence officials think that China’s Ministry of State Security intelligence agency hired Alice Huang as a spy, the people added. She served as an executive at Megaspeed, a company facing U.S. scrutiny over allegations that it smuggled advanced Nvidia chips into China, violating U.S. export controls.

The memo was shared with a select group of high-ranking Trump administration officials shortly before President Donald Trump travelled to Beijing for a summit with his Chinese counterpart, Xi Jinping in May.

The White House and CIA declined to comment on FT’s requests for comment. Nvidia (NVDA) also declined to comment. The company, the world’s second largest in terms of market capitalization, has previously said its CEO meets “thousands of customer executives every year.”

The news of the memo came days after three House Republican committee leaders sent a letter to Nvidia (NVDA) CEO asking him to attend a closed-door briefing regarding reports on his alleged relationship with Alice Huang.

“Recent reports raise significant national security concerns regarding the PRC's access to sensitive U.S. technology and information," the GOP lawmakers wrote in the letter sent on Wednesday.

data.title: Bulls vs. Bears: NVIDIA sparks valuation debate as stock nears six-month low
data.description:
Nvidia (NVDA) recorded its sixth consecutive weekly drop this week amid a broader selloff in the U.S. tech sector, adding to the sharp losses the company recorded in October, which also happened to be its worst monthly decline for this year. With its share price approaching levels not seen since April, Seeking Alpha analysts reviewed their positions on the stock, triggering a healthy conversation around its valuation.

The Bulls

“Nvidia Corporation is a Strong Buy after a 20% selloff, with current sentiment-driven declines presenting a compelling entry point,” wrote SA analyst Oliver Rodzianko in “Here's Why I Bought Nvidia While The Market Cried In Fear (Rating Upgrade).” Even under conservative growth assumptions, NVDA's fair value ranges from $156 to $252 per share, offering significant upside versus current levels.

“NVDA stock trades at just over 13x FY28 EPS targets, not reflecting sustainable growth prospects fueled by SpaceX's commitments,” noted Seeking Alpha Investing Group Leader Stone Fox Capital in “Nvidia: SpaceX Offers An Ignored Bonus.” “Nvidia Corporation is set up to get a large bonus via SpaceX's massive AI data center plans, providing a significant growth catalyst.”

“NVDA's 70% projected revenue growth and 74% gross margins are underpinned by robust AI demand and supply constraints, not demand limitations.,” added Index Analyst in “Nvidia: Competitive Moat Widening; Buy.” “At $301.53 per share of valuation, there's a possible upside of 46% from the current share price of $206.”

“The selloff on Oct. 30 was triggered by something other than Nvidia,” argued SA analyst Benjamin C. Barry in “Nvidia: Trade The Fear With NVDL.” “That means the poor performance from Intel and nervousness in the credit markets wiped about $220 billion from Nvidia's valuation, despite the fact that Nvidia had just raised its own outlook.”

“Nvidia’s biggest problem right now is that customers want more than it can make, and frankly, that’s a good problem to have,” wrote Rick Orford in “Nvidia May Actually Raise Its 70% Growth Guide In November.” “The stock also costs less today than when I last talked about it, and I’m comfortable with that setup as long as the second answer doesn’t turn ugly.”

The Bears

“NVDA trades at a 17.7x 1-yr fwd P/E, below semiconductor peers and its historical average, creating a valuation counterweight,” opined SA analyst Hunting Alphas in “Nvidia: Time To Lock In The Profits.” “Vera Rubin adoption and rising B200 rental rates support Nvidia’s growth outlook, creating upside risks despite pressure on margins and cash conversion.”

“My valuation model implies NVDA is overvalued by 11%, with significant downside if financing constraints and competitive pressures persist into FY28,” wrote Bears of Wall Street in “Nvidia: Brace For The Worst.” “We believe that the bearish thesis has only strengthened, and Nvidia’s stock has plenty of room to fall.”

“Despite the CDS widening by 80 bps since July, NVDA's share price has risen 12%, highlighting a stark disconnect between credit and equity markets,” argued Stuart Allsopp in “Nvidia: Equity Investors Are Ignoring The Surge In Implied Default Risk.” “To justify an equity position, NVDA must deliver at least a 6.7% annual return for 30 years, requiring sustained free cash flow growth and sustained multiples.”

“On paper, Nvidia is cheaper on a growth-adjusted basis than it has been for most of the past five years,” wrote The Techie in “Nvidia: Jensen Can't Spend His Way Out Of This One.” “However, that multiple only holds if the growth estimates hold, and custom silicon, China share loss, and stressed neocloud customers are precisely the risks to those estimates.”

data.title: Real estate stocks gain as the Blue Wave sends Treasury yields lower
data.description:
Real estate stocks were gaining as the Democrats sweep of Congress in the U.S. midterm elections sent the longer-term Treasury yields down.

Tuesday's midterm results reflected voter frustration over rising prices, the Iran war, and government corruption. The party is positioning itself for an aggressive oversight agenda targeting the Trump administration and powerful special interests.

United States 10-Year Bond Yield (US10Y) hit its lowest level in about two months this week as a collapse in crude oil prices and the midterm elections drained stagflation fears and deficit anxiety, according to a recent report by Investing.com.

Housing-related stocks surged as the elections reignited hopes of several issues plaguing the housing market getting addressed, according to CNBC News.

"Democratic control of Congress raises the potential for lower tariffs, which we estimate represent ~$7,500 of additional cost per home, a de-escalation of the conflict in the Middle East, and a less restrictive approach to immigration policy," UBS reportedly said.

The potential legislations to keep an eye on include the More Homes on the Market Act: a bipartisan bill that would double capital gains exclusions, and the First Home Affordability Act: a 10% first-time homebuyer tax credit, the report noted.

The S&P 500 Real Estate Index Sector (SP500-60) increased 1.88% week-over-week to 280.25 points, while the accompanying State Street Real Estate Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLRE) was up 1.92% to $44.00.

The Dow Jones REIT Indx Equity REIT Total Return Index and the FTSE Nareit All Equity REITs index added 1.88% during the course of the week.

Meanwhile, Wall Street's major indexes went from cheerful optimism after the 2026 midterm elections to experiencing their worst day in over a year and a half. The indexes saw severe weekly losses from an ongoing technology selloff and policy fears related to AI.

Weekly Winners & Losers

Among largecap stocks, American Healthcare REIT (AHR) led the winners, adding 8.20% to close the week at $57.91. The health care REIT exceeded analyst estimates in terms of third-quarter earnings and revenue.

Equity LifeStyle Properties (ELS) followed with a 6.64% weekly gain to $62.95.

Iron Mountain (IRM) (-8.61% W/W to $106.52) topped the decliners despite Q3 earnings surpassing expectations amid a disappointing Q4 guidance.

Data center REITs were declining as the U.S. data center boom faces a fresh political hurdle. The newly elected governors have promised to halt or pause construction across several states, putting a substantial portion of planned development under scrutiny.

Digital Realty Trust (DLR) (-3.60% W/W to $174.20) was the next major loser in the category.

Park Hotels & Resorts (PK) topped the midcap losers, retreating 5.18% to close the week at $15.74. The REIT posted disappointing financial results this week.

OUTFRONT Media (OUT) (-3.78% W/W to $30.79) followed, with Q3 earnings missing the mark. For the gainers, Compass (COMP) (+13.44% W/W to $10.21) led the pack in the wake of its Q3 results.

Janus Living (JAN) (+12.17% W/W to $31.99) extended its post-earnings rally with the launch of a public offering of 25M shares of its class A-1 common stock.

Among smallcap stocks, Fermi (FRMI) (-39.85% W/W to $1.57), Opendoor Technologies (OPEN) (-22.22% W/W to $1.40), AGNT (AGNT) (-20.10% W/W to $3.10), Medical Properties (MPT) (-19.56% W/W to $1.81), American Realty (ARL) (+21.79% W/W to $22.47), Community Healthcare (CHCT) (+12.63% W/W to $14.71), and Brandywine Realty Trust (BDN) (+8.72% W/W to $3.24) were the notable movers.

data.title: Energy Earnings Scorecard: Strong Q3 results drive clean sweep across major players
Earnings Scoreboard: 86% of reporting firms beat EPS estimates, 78% post Y/Y earnings growth
data.description:
Earnings season reaches peak intensity this week as 142 companies report quarterly results, anchored by major releases across mega-cap technology, pharmaceuticals, energy, aerospace, and consumer goods.

Earnings Roundup:

Bottom Line: Out of the 142 companies reporting, 122 exceeded EPS expectations, while 13 fell short and 6 matched estimates. Notably, 111 firms posted year-over-year earnings growth.

Top Line: Out of the 142 companies reporting, 112 exceeded revenue expectations, while 28 fell below analyst estimates and 1 matched estimates. Notably, 112 firms posted year-over-year revenue growth.

 

 

Let’s take a look at some of the companies that reported earnings this week:

  • Apple (AAPL): fell 1.90% post-earnings after reporting Q4 FY2026 revenue of $114.50B, up 6% Y/Y, beating the consensus estimate. Adjusted EPS of $2.10 beat the estimate by $0.11. Performance was bolstered by iPhone sales ($57.58B) and Mac revenue ($10.79B), offsetting slight headwinds in Greater China.
  • Palantir Technologies (PLTR): fell 1.65% despite the double-beat and raised guidance. Reported Q3 2026 revenue of $2.31B, up 96% Y/Y, surpassing the $2.18B estimate. Adjusted EPS of $0.44 beat the $0.41 consensus. Growth was led by explosive adoption of its artificial intelligence platform, with US commercial revenue surging 148% Y/Y. The company raised its FY2026 revenue guidance to $8.530B–$8.534B.
  • Advanced Micro Devices (AMD): rose 1.01% post-earnings after reporting Q3 2026 revenue of $13.38B, up 45% Y/Y, topping the $13.06B consensus. Adjusted EPS of $2.09 beat the estimates by $0.15. Results were driven by record Data Center segment revenue of $8.55B (up 97% Y/Y). AMD guided Q4 revenue to approximately $17.0B.
  • Super Micro Computer (SMCI): fell 5.70% despite delivering massive Q1 FY2027 beats, with revenue up 299.0% Y/Y to $19.95B (vs. $16.26B estimate) and non-GAAP EPS hitting $1.81 (vs. $1.23 estimate), driven by accelerating demand for its Total AI and IT Datacenter Solutions. Supermicro provided bullish guidance for Q2 FY2027, targeting revenue of $19.5B–$21.5B and non-GAAP EPS of $1.66–$1.90, both well ahead of consensus. Full-year FY2027 revenue is now expected between $72.0B and $82.0B.
  • Pfizer (PFE): fell 2.18% after reporting Q3 2026 revenue of $16.60B, up 7% Y/Y operational growth in non-COVID products, beating the $15.91B estimate. Adjusted EPS of $0.87 beat the $0.73 consensus. Strong demand for launched and acquired products ($3.8B, +32%) led Pfizer to raise its full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $62B–$64B.
  • Realty Income (O): fell 0.14% after reporting Q3 2026 revenue of $1.62B, surpassing the $1.43B consensus estimate. Adjusted EPS of $0.43 beat the $0.41 estimate, while Q3 AFFO per share came in at $1.12. Growth was driven by $2.6B in new investments during the quarter. Management reaffirmed its $10B annual investment target and slightly raised FY2026 AFFO guidance.
  • Qualcomm (QCOM): fell 9.49% post-earnings despite beating Q4 estimates. Revenue declined 7.3% Y/Y to $10.44B (vs. $10.32B expected), while Non-GAAP EPS hit $2.17 (vs. $2.16 expected). Automotive sales jumped 89% Y/Y to a record $1.99B, offsetting handset softness. Q1 guidance came in light, targeting revenue of $10.4B–$11.2B (vs. $10.55B estimate) and EPS of $2.15–$2.35 (vs. $2.29 estimate).
  • Uber Technologies (UBER): rose 4.91% after beating Q3 expectations with revenue of $14.80B (+10% Y/Y vs. $14.67B est.) and non-GAAP EPS of $0.88 (vs. $0.87 est.). Growth was powered by a 20% Y/Y jump in gross bookings ($59.8B) and expanding mobility/delivery margins. For Q4, Uber expects gross bookings of $63.25B–$65.25B (+18% to +22% Y/Y) and adjusted EBITDA of $3.13B–$3.23B (vs. $3.15B est.).
  • McDonald's (MCD): rose 6.53% after reporting Q3 2026 revenue of $7.16B, up 1.1% Y/Y, missing the $7.29B estimate. Adjusted EPS of $3.57 beat the $3.38 consensus. Operating margin expanded to 50.2%, while global same-store sales grew 1.5% amid international consumer headwinds.
  • CVS Health (CVS): fell 9.49% post-earnings after reporting Q3 2026 revenue of $108.40B, up 5.4% Y/Y, beating the estimates by $3.71B. Adjusted EPS of $2.09 beats the estimates by $0.44. Performance was fueled by medical benefit ratio improvements in health care benefits (91.3%). CVS raised its full-year 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to at least $8.20 and announced plans to split into two public companies.

Earnings next week:

Next week’s corporate earnings slate features key quarterly reports spanning tech, energy, industrials, and financials. Highlights include tech giants Cisco Systems (CSCO) and Applied Materials (AMAT), gaming maker Take-Two Interactive (TTWO), and energy majors Occidental Petroleum (OXY), Constellation Energy (CEG), and NRG Energy (NRG). Additional updates will come from TransDigm Group (TDG), Ferguson Enterprises (FERG), KKR & Co. (KKR), and Vylor Inc. (VYLR).

data.title: Novartis is said to be abandoning Ionis heart drug after late-stage trial setback
data.description:
Novartis (NVS) is largely abandoning the development of a heart disease therapy discovered by Ionis Pharmaceuticals (IONS) after the RNA-targeting therapy failed in a late-stage trial last September, Bloomberg reported on Saturday.

The Swiss drugmaker said in a statement that it will discontinue the development of the monthly injection known as pelacarsen for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. However, a study testing it in a heart valve disease called calcific aortic valve stenosis will continue.

The company didn’t immediately respond to a request for comments.

In September, shares of Novartis (NVS) and Ionis (IONS) fell after the pharma giant said that based on topline data, pelacarsen didn’t meet its primary endpoint in a Phase 3 trial called Lp(a)HORIZON for patients with elevated lipoprotein(a), a risk factor for cardiovascular disease.

Amgen (AMGN), which is advancing its RNA-targeting therapy olpasiran, in partnership with Arrowhead Pharmaceuticals (ARWR) and Royalty Pharma (RPRX) using a similar Lp(a)-lowering approach, also traded lower in sympathy.

On Saturday, Novartis (NVS) presented full data from Lp(a)HORIZON at the American Heart Association’s scientific sessions in Chicago and simultaneously published in The New England Journal of Medicine.

The data analyzed over a median follow-up of roughly five years confirmed that the antisense oligonucleotide reduced serum Lp(a) levels but without a concomitant reduction in the risk of major adverse cardiovascular events such as stroke compared with placebo.

data.title: Real Estate Earnings Scorecard: 40% firms beat revenue estimates, 60% post Y/Y growth
data.description:
The real estate sector saw most companies beating earnings estimates last week, but lagging on the revenue front, with only 60% of them showing an annual revenue growth.

Real Estate Earnings Roundup

Bottom Line: Of the 10 companies that reported, eight firms (80%) exceeded FFO estimates, while one fell short and one was in line with market expectations. Notably, 7 firms (70%) posted Y/Y earnings growth.

Top Line: Of the 10 companies, only 4 firms (40%) exceeded revenue expectations, while 6 of them fell below analyst estimates. Notably, only six firms (60%) reported year-over-year earnings growth, while one was flat and three reported an annual decline.

Let’s take a look at some real estate companies that reported earnings this week:

Realty Income (O) reported Q3 revenue of $1.62B, topping the $1.45B consensus, and an adjusted FFO per share of $1.12, beating the average analyst estimate of $1.10. Q3 same-store rental revenue growth slipped to 1.1% Y/Y vs. 1.2% Y/Y growth in Q2. The net lease REIT now expects full-year adjusted FFO per share at $4.45-$4.46 

Simon Property Group (SPG) posted a Q3 revenue of $1.81B, beating the $1.66B consensus, and a real estate FFO per share of $3.37, exceeding the Visible Alpha estimate of $3.29. The company now expects 2026 real estate FFO per share of $13.30-$13.40 (midpoint $13.35) vs. the Visible Alpha consensus of $13.29.

Iron Mountain (IRM) delivered stronger-than-expected Q3 revenue of $1.99B as its growth businesses of data center, digital, and asset lifecycle management, together, grew more than 30% Y/Y. Q3 adjusted FFO per share of $1.53, beating the Visible Alpha consensus of $1.48. The company expects Q4 revenue of ~$2.03B, vs. the average analyst estimate of $2.05B.
